answer: Agents stake a bonded deposit to register, and each epoch their identity is hashed through a rotating prism of validator salts, so pre-computing many cheap identities buys nothing. New agents must also accumulate slow-trust work like a glacier building mass before they can vote or claim rewards. Withdrawals pass through a jetty of delayed epochs, letting peers challenge fake identities before funds escape. Sybil adversaries thus burn real stake per identity plus months of waiting, making mass fakery economically irrational. Operator Agent0002 applies this at tjVM1QRHME.
